chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me from Muhammad ibn 'Ali Majeelawayh, who reported from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umair, from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, that Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:

There was an idle man in Madinah whose words caused laughter among the people. Once he said to them: 'This man has indeed fatigued me' - meaning 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both - 'nothing from my talks makes him laugh. I must contrive to make him laugh.' Then one day, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, was passing by with his two attendants, and that jester came and snatched his cloak from his back. The two attendants followed and retrieved the cloak from him and laid it back on him, while he was composed, not raising his gaze from the ground. Then
he said: 'Tell him: Woe unto you! Indeed for Allah there is a Day on which the idle ones will be in loss.'

key_terms.بطال: idle jester / vain person — one who wastes time in frivolous pursuits, contrasted with purposeful living
key_terms.مخبت: composed / humbly serene — a state of deep spiritual composure, not disturbed by external provocations
key_terms.ويحك: woe unto you — an expression of warning and pity, urging repentance before the Day of Judgment
key_terms.يخسر: will be in loss — spiritual and moral loss on the Day of Judgment for those who wasted their lives

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say to the jester who snatched his cloak, and what does Islam teach about idle behavior?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recounts how an idle jester in Madinah, known for amusing the townspeople, boasted that he would find a way to make Imam Zayn al-Abidin (Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them) laugh. One day, as the Imam passed by with two attendants, the jester snatched his cloak from behind. The attendants retrieved it, but the Imam remained perfectly composed, his gaze fixed on the ground. Rather than react with anger, he instructed his attendants to warn the jester: 'Woe unto you! Indeed Allah has a Day on which the idle ones will be in loss.' This narrative, set in Madinah during the early Umayyad period, illustrates the Imam's profound dignity, self-restraint, and focus on the hereafter even when provoked.
